concepts.name: Binary signals and logic levels
concepts.summary: Recall that digital circuits represent information as two levels, 0 and 1, and relate them to voltage ranges.

concepts.name: Basic gate functions
concepts.summary: Explain what AND, OR and NOT gates output for each input combination and recognise their symbols.

concepts.name: Truth tables
concepts.summary: Write and read a truth table listing every input combination and the resulting output of a gate or small circuit.

concepts.name: Derived gates NAND NOR XOR
concepts.summary: Describe the behaviour of NAND, NOR, XOR and XNOR gates and how they relate to the basic gates.

concepts.name: Boolean expressions
concepts.summary: Interpret expressions using AND, OR and complement notation as descriptions of gate networks.

concepts.name: Number systems for logic
concepts.summary: Convert between binary, decimal and hexadecimal to label input and output patterns.

misconceptions.text: The logic value 1 always means exactly 5 volts.
An OR gate outputs 1 only when exactly one input is 1.
A NAND gate is simply an AND gate with the inputs inverted.

concepts.name: Boolean algebra laws
concepts.summary: Apply identity, complement, distributive and absorption laws to rewrite expressions.

concepts.name: De Morgan's theorems
concepts.summary: Use De Morgan's theorems to convert between AND-type and OR-type forms and to push inversions through gates.

concepts.name: Sum of products and product of sums
concepts.summary: Derive canonical SOP and POS expressions from a truth table using minterms and maxterms.

concepts.name: Circuit from expression
concepts.summary: Draw a gate network from a Boolean expression and evaluate its output for given inputs.

concepts.name: NAND-only and NOR-only implementation
concepts.summary: Rebuild a network using only NAND or only NOR gates.

concepts.name: Karnaugh maps up to four variables
concepts.summary: Fill a K-map from a truth table and group adjacent ones in powers of two to get a minimal SOP.

concepts.name: Don't-care conditions
concepts.summary: Use don't-care entries in K-maps to enlarge groups and simplify the result.

misconceptions.text: De Morgan's theorem says the complement of A AND B equals the complement of A AND the complement of B.
K-map groups can be any size as long as they contain only ones.
K-map rows and columns are ordered in plain binary counting order.

concepts.name: Quine-McCluskey minimisation
concepts.summary: Find prime and essential prime implicants systematically for functions with many variables.

concepts.name: Multiplexers and decoders
concepts.summary: Design and use multiplexers, decoders and encoders, including implementing functions with a MUX.

concepts.name: Half and full adders
concepts.summary: Build half and full adders and chain them into a multi-bit ripple-carry adder.

concepts.name: Two's complement arithmetic circuits
concepts.summary: Analyse how adders perform signed addition and subtraction and detect overflow.

concepts.name: Propagation delay and hazards
concepts.summary: Analyse how gate delays create glitches and how redundant terms remove static hazards.

concepts.name: SR and D latches
concepts.summary: Explain and trace cross-coupled gate latches and the transparent D latch, including the forbidden SR state.

concepts.name: Edge-triggered flip-flops
concepts.summary: Distinguish latches from edge-triggered D, JK and T flip-flops and predict outputs from timing diagrams.

concepts.name: Combinational HDL description
concepts.summary: Describe combinational circuits in Verilog or VHDL using continuous assignments and simple processes.

misconceptions.text: A latch and a flip-flop are the same thing.
A hazard-free minimal SOP is always obtained by choosing the fewest terms.
Carry out of the top bit always signals overflow in signed addition.

concepts.name: Synchronous counter design
concepts.summary: Design synchronous counters from flip-flop excitation tables and compare them with ripple counters.

concepts.name: Registers and shift registers
concepts.summary: Analyse register structures with load, enable and shift control, and their use in data paths.

concepts.name: Finite state machine modelling
concepts.summary: Model sequential behaviour as Moore or Mealy machines with state diagrams and transition tables.

concepts.name: State assignment and implementation
concepts.summary: Choose state encodings and derive next-state and output logic, evaluating cost and speed trade-offs.

concepts.name: Setup hold and clock timing
concepts.summary: Calculate setup and hold slack and maximum clock frequency from flip-flop and logic delays.

concepts.name: Synthesisable sequential HDL
concepts.summary: Write and evaluate HDL for registers and FSMs that synthesise to the intended hardware, avoiding inferred latches.

concepts.name: Testbenches and simulation
concepts.summary: Build testbenches that exercise a design and judge correctness from simulated waveforms.

misconceptions.text: A Mealy machine and a Moore machine always need the same number of states and respond at the same time.
Lowering the clock frequency fixes both setup and hold violations.
Blocking and nonblocking assignments are interchangeable in clocked HDL code.

concepts.name: Metastability and synchronisers
concepts.summary: Evaluate metastability risk and design safe clock domain crossings using synchronisers and handshakes.

concepts.name: Fast adder architectures
concepts.summary: Compare carry-lookahead, carry-select and prefix adders on delay and area.

concepts.name: Datapath and control partitioning
concepts.summary: Design a system by separating datapath and FSM controller from an algorithmic specification.

concepts.name: Pipelining and retiming
concepts.summary: Insert pipeline stages and retime logic to raise clock rate while weighing latency, area and hazards.

concepts.name: Clocking and power trade-offs
concepts.summary: Assess clock skew, gating and dynamic power effects on timing and reliability.

concepts.name: Design for testability and verification
concepts.summary: Plan scan, assertions and coverage-driven verification so that a design can be tested and proven correct.

concepts.name: Synthesis and implementation trade-offs
concepts.summary: Judge how synthesis constraints and target technology affect area, speed and structure, and restructure RTL accordingly.

misconceptions.text: A two-flop synchroniser eliminates metastability completely.
Pipelining always improves overall performance because it shortens the clock period.
Passing simulation proves a design is correct and ready for hardware.
